ideas.question: Does pregnancy weight gain differ between SUID cases and mothers of live births?
ideas.comparison: ncfrp_v51 (case series) compared with prams_p8_std2 (population reference); cdc_natl15 (denominator)
ideas.why_open: This question aims to explore whether there is a significant difference in pregnancy weight gain between mothers who experienced SUID and those who did not, which could potentially indicate unmeasured risk factors or behavioral differences.
ideas.data: Case series (ncfrp_v51:INF4mombmi) records the pregnancy weight gain of mothers who experienced SUID, while population reference (prams_p8_std2 and prams_p7_arf:PREGWTGAIN or PREG_WKGAIN) provides the weighted prevalence of pregnancy weight gain among a representative sample of live births.

ideas.question: Are there differences in maternal stressors between SUID cases and the general population?
ideas.comparison: ncfrp_v51 (case series) compared with prams_p8_arf (population reference); cdc_natl15 (denominator)
ideas.why_open: By comparing the prevalence of maternal stressors, this research could shed light on whether certain stressful life events or conditions disproportionately affect mothers who experience SUID.
ideas.data: Case series (ncfrp_v51:INFstressor) captures maternal stressors among mothers who experienced SUID, while population reference (prams_p8_arf and prams_p7_arf:D100) provides weighted prevalence of these same stressors in a representative sample of live births.

ideas.question: How do health care visits during pregnancy differ between SUID cases and the general population?
ideas.comparison: ncfrp_v51 (case series) compared with prams_p8_arf (population reference); cdc_natl15 (denominator)
ideas.why_open: Investigating healthcare utilization can reveal whether inadequate or excessive use of health care during pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of SUID.
ideas.data: Case series (ncfrp_v51:PREG_VISIT) captures prenatal healthcare visits among mothers who experienced SUID, while population reference (prams_p8_arf and prams_p7_arf:HEALTHCARE_VISITS_DURING_PREGNANCY) provides weighted prevalence of these health care visits in a representative sample.

ideas.question: What is the difference in postpartum contraception use between mothers who experienced SUID and those who did not?
ideas.comparison: ncfrp_v51 (case series) compared with prams_p8_arf, prams_p7_arf (population reference); cdc_natl15 (denominator)
ideas.why_open: This comparison can highlight whether the use of postpartum contraception differs between mothers who experienced SUID and those who did not.
ideas.data: Case series (ncfrp_v51:BCMETHOD) captures postpartum contraception use among mothers who experienced SUID, while population reference (prams_p8_arf and prams_p7_arf:BIRTH_CONTROL_USAGE) provides weighted prevalence of these methods in a representative sample.

ideas.question: Is there an association between substance abuse during pregnancy and the incidence of SUID?
ideas.comparison: ncfrp_v51 (case series) compared with prams_p8_arf, prams_p7_arf (population reference); cdc_natl15 (denominator)
ideas.why_open: This question seeks to understand whether substance abuse during pregnancy is more common among mothers who experienced SUID compared to those who did not.
ideas.data: Case series (ncfrp_v51:INFdruguse) captures substance use among mothers who experienced SUID, while population reference (prams_p8_arf and prams_p7_arf:D309) provides weighted prevalence of these behaviors in a representative sample.
